C2.title: The investment club
C2.brief: Kabir has brought a fictional phone to the kiosk. Inspect the conversations, identify the pressure tactics, and rebuild what happened. No real money is used.
C2.closing: Case closed. You checked the evidence, named the tactics, and chose a safer response.
C2.debrief.mechanism: The sender creates a story, adds pressure, discourages outside checks, and asks for money or account access.
C2.debrief.c1: Pause before responding to a message that creates pressure.
C2.debrief.c2: Verify the claim through a contact you find independently.
C2.debrief.c3: Protect your payment details and ask a trusted person for help.
C2-E01: Guaranteed profit of ten percent every day. No chance of loss.
C2-01.explain: Certainty and extraordinary returns are used as bait. A screenshot is not proof of an investment.
C2-L1.q: Which detail in the phone shows an easy reward?
C2-L1.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.
C2-E02: Our group admin is an approved investment officer. Trust the badge in this profile.
C2-02.explain: A profile badge and a title do not establish credentials. Verify independently.
C2-L2.q: Which detail in the phone shows a claimed identity?
C2-L2.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.
C2-E03: The profit slot closes in five minutes. Transfer before it is gone.
C2-03.explain: A short deadline pushes a decision without independent research.
C2-L3.q: Which detail in the phone shows time pressure?
C2-L3.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.
C2-E04: Keep the strategy confidential. Do not discuss it outside this group.
C2-04.explain: Isolation prevents an independent person from questioning the story.
C2-L4.q: Which detail in the phone shows secrecy?
C2-L4.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.
C2-E05: Transfer Rs. 2,000 to unlock your withdrawal.
C2-05.explain: An extra payment demanded to release supposed profit is another attempt to take money.

C2-L5.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.
C2-E06: Install our access app and share your screen while you open the bank app.
C2-06.explain: Sharing device access can expose financial information. Do not grant it to an unknown caller.
C2-L6.q: Which detail in the phone shows a request for money or access?
C2-L6.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.

C2.fix.q: What is the safest next step?
C2.fix.safe: Stop the conversation, verify independently, and ask a trusted person for help.
C2.fix.safe.why: This removes the pressure and gives you a reliable way to check the request.
C2.fix.pay: Send the money first and check later.
C2.fix.pay.why: Sending money first gives the sender what they want before the claim is verified.
C2.fix.share: Share the requested account details to settle the matter.
C2.fix.share.why: Account secrets and device access should stay private, regardless of the story.
C2.replay.1: The sender starts a story to attract attention.
C2.replay.2: A claimed identity or frightening statement makes the story feel important.
C2.replay.3: A deadline creates pressure to act.
C2.replay.5: The sender asks for money, secrets, or control of the device.
